```json
 "topology": "NMOS-input folded cascode (single stage) with resistor-referenced cascode biasing",
 "rationale": "A single stage at CL=1pF needs gm1≈1.3-1.6 mS for 150 MHz+ GBW. I1≈120uA at gm/Id 13 gives that. The cascoded output gives 55-65 dB. The folding pole is about 4x GBW and the mirror pole is above 1.5 GHz, so PM is ~70°. Supply current is ~2(I1+Ic)+bias ≈ 430 uA, about 0.8 mW, well under 2 mW. The NMOS input suits VCM=0.9 V. CS Vds is about 0.3 V, set by resistors in the cascode-bias diodes."}
```

```python
PARAMS = {
    "gmid1": (13.0, 9.0, 18.0),     # input pair gm/Id
    "L1":    (0.3, 0.15, 0.8),      # input pair L
    "I1":    (120e-6, 70e-6, 220e-6),  # per-side input current
    "kc":    (0.6, 0.3, 1.2),       # cascode branch current / I1
    "gmidpc":(12.0, 8.0, 15.0),     # PMOS cascode gm/Id
    "Lpc":   (0.3, 0.15, 0.8),      # PMOS cascode L
    "Lcs":   (0.5, 0.3, 1.5),       # PMOS current-source L
    "Lnm":   (0.5, 0.3, 1.5),       # NMOS bottom mirror L
    "vcs":   (0.30, 0.22, 0.40),    # Vds reserved for CS devices (IR drop in bias diodes)
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    VDD = 1.8
    cl = spec.get("cl", 1e-12); iref = spec.get("iref", 10e-6)
    I1 = p["I1"]; Ic = p["kc"] * I1; Ip = I1 + Ic; It = 2 * I1
    vcs = p["vcs"]
    Ib1 = 20e-6; Ib2 = 10e-6; Ib3 = 10e-6

    # devices
    mb0 = lut.size("n", 10, 1.0, iref, vds=0.6)                         # ibias diode
    m0  = lut.size("n", 10, 1.0, It, vds=0.25)                          # tail
    mbn1 = lut.size("n", 10, 1.0, Ib1, vds=0.8)
    mbn2 = lut.size("n", 10, 1.0, Ib2, vds=0.5)
    m1  = lut.size("n", p["gmid1"], p["L1"], I1, vds=1.2, vsb=0.25)    # input pair
    m3  = lut.size("p", 10, p["Lcs"], Ip, vds=vcs)                      # PMOS CS sources
    mpb = lut.size("p", 10, p["Lcs"], Ib1, vds=m3.vgs)                  # PMOS bias diode
    mpb2 = lut.size("p", 10, p["Lcs"], Ib3, vds=0.6)                    # feeds vnc branch
    m5  = lut.size("p", p["gmidpc"], p["Lpc"], Ic, vds=0.6, vsb=vcs)   # PMOS cascodes
    mpcb = lut.size("p", p["gmidpc"], p["Lpc"], Ib2, vds=m5.vgs, vsb=vcs)
    m7  = lut.size("n", 12, 0.5, Ic, vds=0.5, vsb=vcs)                  # NMOS cascodes
    mncb = lut.size("n", 12, 0.5, Ib3, vds=m7.vgs, vsb=vcs)
    m9  = lut.size("n", 10, p["Lnm"], Ic, vds=vcs)                      # bottom mirror

    n = Netlist("vinp vinn vout vdd vss ibias")
    # bias
    n.dev("MB0", "ibias", "ibias", "vss", "vss", mb0)
    n.dev("M0", "tail", "ibias", "vss", "vss", m0)
    n.dev("MBN1", "vpb", "ibias", "vss", "vss", mbn1)
    n.dev("MPB", "vpb", "vpb", "vdd", "vdd", mpb)
    n.dev("MBN2", "vpc", "ibias", "vss", "vss", mbn2)
    n.R("RPC", "vdd", "xpc", vcs / Ib2)
    n.dev("MPCB", "vpc", "vpc", "xpc", "vdd", mpcb)
    n.dev("MPB2", "vnc", "vpb", "vdd", "vdd", mpb2)
    n.dev("MNCB", "vnc", "vnc", "xnc", "vss", mncb)
    n.R("RNC", "xnc", "vss", vcs / Ib3)
    # input pair (vinp -> drives fold node on output side for non-inverting)
    n.dev("M1", "f1", "vinn", "tail", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("M2", "f2", "vinp", "tail", "vss", m1)
    # PMOS current sources
    n.dev("M3", "f1", "vpb", "vdd", "vdd", m3)
    n.dev("M4", "f2", "vpb", "vdd", "vdd", m3)
    # PMOS cascodes
    n.dev("M5", "nm", "vpc", "f1", "vdd", m5)
    n.dev("M6", "vout", "vpc", "f2", "vdd", m5)
    # NMOS cascoded mirror
    n.dev("M7", "nm", "vnc", "n9", "vss", m7)
    n.dev("M8", "vout", "vnc", "n10", "vss", m7)
    n.dev("M9", "n9", "nm", "vss", "vss", m9)
    n.dev("M10", "n10", "nm", "vss", "vss", m9)

    # predictions
    # vinp up -> M2 current up -> f2 down... current into vout from M6 decreases -> vout down?
    # M2 draws more from f2 => less current through M6 into vout; M1 draws less => more through M5 -> mirror sinks more
    # => vout falls: so vinp would be inverting. Swap handled below by naming check.
    ro_up = m5.gm / m5.gds / (m3.gds + m1.gds)
    ro_dn = m7.gm / m7.gds / m9.gds
    rout = 1 / (1 / ro_up + 1 / ro_dn)
    A0 = m1.gm * rout
    ctot = cl + m5.cdd + m7.cdd
    gbw = m1.gm / (2 * PI * ctot)
    cf = m1.cdd + m3.cdd + m5.cgg
    pf = m5.gm / (2 * PI * cf)
    cm = 2 * m9.cgg + m7.cdd + m5.cdd
    pm_ = m9.gm / (2 * PI * cm)
    pm = 90 - math.degrees(math.atan(gbw / pf)) - 0.5 * math.degrees(math.atan(gbw / pm_))
    power = VDD * (2 * Ip + iref + Ib1 + Ib2 + Ib3)
    return n, {"gain_db": db(A0), "ugbw": gbw, "pm": pm, "power": power}
```

Polarity check: raising vinp raises M2 current, which pulls f2 down. That cuts the current M6 delivers into vout. Raising vinp also lowers M1 current, so more current flows through M5 into nm. The mirror (M9/M10) then sinks more from vout, and vout falls.

That makes vinp, as wired above, the inverting input. To fix it, the gates are swapped so that vinp drives M1 (the f1/mirror side). Use this corrected input-pair block:

```python
    n.dev("M1", "f1", "vinp", "tail", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("M2", "f2", "vinn", "tail", "vss", m1)
```

With this swap, raising vinp lowers the f1-branch current into nm, so the mirror sinks less, and it also raises M6's current into vout. Both effects push vout up, so vinp is the non-inverting input.

Replace the two `M1`/`M2` lines in the program with these. The rest of the program is unchanged.
